prompt: The old-project-q3 channel belongs to our workspace, and we're doing a permissions review before we finish archiving related channels. Which of our workspace members currently hold admin-level roles in that same workspace?
binding_note: r0 (user_teams, the membership) and r2 (channels, containing old-project-q3) both share team_id equal to r1.team_id (teams), so the membership's workspace is required to be the same workspace that contains the named channel; the admin-role condition is then applied to r0 within that bound workspace.

roles.reason: The exact-named conversation used to identify the relevant workspace via the CONVERSATION node.

roles.facts: team_id T01WORKSPACE, team_name 'Test Workspace'; contains old-project-q3 and all its channels/members.
roles.reason: The WORKSPACE node joining membership to conversation.
Workspace membership with admin role in the same workspace that contains old-project-q3.
Second workspace membership with admin role in the same workspace as old-project-q3.
Same workspace as old-project-q3, but role is member, not admin, so excluded by the role condition.
Another same-workspace membership with non-admin role, excluded on the same basis.

roles.facts: New team_id T02BETA, team_name 'Beta Testers Guild', added as a distinct workspace unrelated to old-project-q3.
roles.reason: Provides a genuinely different workspace so the WORKSPACE join is not vacuously satisfied by only one team existing.
A channel in the other workspace, contrasting with old-project-q3's workspace.

roles.facts: New user U_ZOE ('Zoe Chen'), team_id=T02BETA, role=admin.
roles.reason: Holds an admin role, but in the Beta Testers Guild workspace, not the workspace containing old-project-q3, so the CONVERSATION-bound WORKSPACE join excludes it.

obligations.name: workspace_admin_memberships
obligations.description: The workspace-membership records with an admin role, restricted to the workspace that contains the old-project-q3 channel.
obligations.scope: workspace memberships in the workspace containing the named channel, filtered to admin role

task_spec.text: Identify the workspace that contains the old-project-q3 channel, then list the members of that workspace who hold an admin role.

access_plan: Use conversations.list (or conversations.info with the known channel name) to find old-project-q3 and read its team_id. Then use users.list scoped to that team_id and users.info per user to read each user's workspace role (owner/admin/member, derived from user_teams.role), filtering for admin-level roles.
